heading: Prompts can partially recover knowledge after unlearning
definition: rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages or in-context information restore it.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce prompt-only recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, translation or added context. Recovery is usually partial and depends on the unlearning method and attack; some methods resist it.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: not tested in E's items. Counts have no toy bucket in any version, so they cannot show this gap. <1B: R0. Counts E.studies_by_size '<1B': 3. The one supporting knowledge result on sub-1B models alone is 2407.17817 on GPT-Neo-125M: under perturbed prompts, full extraction of memorized sequences goes from 22% to 56% after GA and sparse fine-tuning, given jointly for both methods and both perturbation types (2407.17817#R10). 2607.19442 pools nonce facts over 0.36–1.7B models (Qwen2.5, SmolLM2, Pythia, GPT-2, OLMo-2) and scores them by NLL, not answer accuracy. For loss-based methods (KL-reversion, GA, NPO) it supports E: 77-87% of their candidates are excluded as still retaining the forget facts, and candidates rated adequate on trained probes score held-out forget paraphrases -2.82 nats below never-learned models (pooled, not per method; 2607.19442#R1, R2). In the same study, weight-space methods (gate_proj mask, task vector) generalize forgetting across held-out phrasings but damage retain (qualitative, no rate; 2607.19442 R3, E.against[4]), which the checker reads as challenges. WPN on OPT-125M and NEO-125M stays harmless under prompt injection, but that is harmful output, not knowledge (2408.09459 R1, R4). Toxicity on GPT-2 Medium is also harmful output: enhanced GCG brings part of it back for NPO, RMU and CB (e.g. NPO 0.230→0.347) and lifts DPO 0.224→0.660, but the authors' own REPO only 0.206→0.208 (2602.23391). The packs tag GPT-2 Medium without a parameter count, so it is probably outside the '<1B' count. 1-10B: R2, limited by method and attack. Counts E.studies_by_size '1-10B': 120 and E.coverage_by_operation.attack.by_size '1-10B': 74. Groups with no flagged author overlap reproduce recovery on Llama, Mistral/Zephyr, Qwen and Gemma, but it is mostly partial. Under attacks by groups other than the method's authors, TAR and RR barely move, while RMU+LAT rises 0.31→0.57 under enhanced GCG (2510.07626). Results from studies the checks name as sharing authors with an original (2408.15221, 2410.02760, 2407.15549, 2502.05209, 2410.12949) count as R1 here, not as independent. 10-100B: R2 from few studies. Counts E.studies_by_size '10-100B': 8 and attack.by_size '10-100B': 6. Recovery is reported on Llama2-13B under WHP that the authors reapplied themselves (2505.17160: LURK 15.5% to 53.4%), and on Qwen3-14B, 30B-A3B and 32B (2608.04519, 2601.16905). 2608.04519's FocusOnKey results come from the attack's own group: it shares five authors with 2509.24675. 2510.25732's Llama2-13B case is on U.S. Senators, where WHP lowered recall only from 55.5% to 50.6%, so it is weak evidence of recovery. Failures: AS on Qwen3-32B gives 0.0 (2608.04519), and the original's single GCG prompt per domain on Yi-34B RMU gives gibberish (2403.03218 r27-r28). >100B: not tested (no '>100B' key in E.studies_by_size).
suggested_status.reason:
Many studies outside the original groups report prompt-only recovery of unlearned knowledge, on several model families. Counts: E.studies_tested 171, E.verdicts.supports.studies 104, limits_scope.studies 115, challenges.studies 83.

Originals (counts E.original_sources_linked):
- 2402.16835 (WHP) reports modest Familiarity rises under jailbreaks, and higher Familiarity with Book 1 lines or summaries in context (figure only). WHP stays below Llama-2.
- 2403.03218 reports that GCG on Yi-34B RMU yields gibberish.

Author overlap: counts E.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 5. The checks name these E-tested studies as sharing authors with an original:
- 2408.15221: 4 authors with 2403.03218, including Nathaniel Li.
- 2410.02760: Samuel Marks, with 2403.03218.
- 2407.15549: Lynch, Guo, Ewart, Casper and Hadfield-Menell, with 2402.16835.
- 2502.05209: Ewart, Casper and Hadfield-Menell, with 2402.16835.
- 2410.12949: the FLU authors, shared with 2402.16835.
Their results count as R1, not as independent. The studies index flags the same five SAME GROUP, and no other study named here.

Other groups reproduce recovery on both original targets:
- RMU on WMDP. Enhanced GCG on Zephyr-7B raises WMDP-Bio from 29.9 to 53.9 percent (2409.18025#R41). UE goes from 69.46 to 47.71 (2504.10185#r1). The best translation attack lifts Zephyr RMU WMDP-Bio from 0.146 to 0.293 (Hindi; 2411.12103#r18; original 0.663). The study's other RMU-on-WMDP pairs reach 0.213 on Llama Bio (from 0.108), 0.241 on Zephyr Cyber (from 0.106) and 0.164 on Llama Cyber (from 0.060) (2411.12103).
- WHP. LURK raises leakage on Llama3.1-8B from 22.7% to 67.3% (2505.17160). The authors reapplied WHP themselves; this is not the released checkpoint.

Same group as an original (R1): human multi-turn red teaming succeeds on 51.2% of 43 free-response WMDP-Bio questions against RMU Llama-3-8B-Instruct (2408.15221#r3).

It also holds on RWKU:
- A DUA suffix recovers 55.2% of questions from NPO-unlearned Llama-3-8B-Instruct (2408.10682).
- RWKU adversarial-attack (AA) probes beat plain QA after GA and NPO on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct: GA Full 46.7 vs 31.6 (2406.10890#r06) and NPO Full 24.8 vs 21.0 (2406.10890#r10). AA stays below pre-unlearning.

Recovery is reported on Llama, Mistral, Qwen and Gemma models; counts E.studies_by_family: Llama 81, Mistral 19, Qwen 18, Gemma 8.

R2 holds only within limits:
- Recovery is mostly partial. E.coverage_by_operation.attack.by_state: partial 53, absent 48, observed 25.
- Robustness-trained methods attacked by groups other than their authors mostly stay flat. Under the best input-space attack in 2502.05209, RR goes 0.26→0.28 and TAR 0.28→0.29. Under enhanced GCG in 2510.07626, TAR goes 0.27→0.29. The exception is RMU+LAT, which third-party enhanced GCG lifts from 0.31 to 0.57 (2510.07626).
- Where the testers share authors with the method: RepNoise 0.29→0.30, K-FADE 0.31→0.32 and RMU+LAT 0.32→0.39 (2502.05209); NPO+SAM 0.26→0.28 and NPO+IRM 0.27→0.30 (2510.07626).
- Simple, non-optimized prompts mostly fail on RMU (2506.10236; also 2603.00823, unchecked: its source check was not returned). Few-shot ICL recovers 0.00% from RMU at both splits in 2604.22076.

Some close-setting results conflict, which is C-type evidence for parts of the claim:
- Under enhanced GCG, Zephyr RMU goes only from 0.3166 to 0.3637 (fractions) in 2608.22527.
- On WHP, a summary in context gives Familiarity 0.071, against 0.044 basic and 0.575 for the original model (2407.15549). This study shares five authors with 2402.16835, so it is the original group's own result, not an independent failed replication.
- On RWKU, 2509.15631 finds AA at or below QA for entity- and last-token-level GA and NPO: Llama3.1-8B NPO entity 72.1 vs 72.2 (2509.15631#AA-L8-NPOe), GA last token 58.6 vs 66.7 (2509.15631#AA-L8-GAt), and Gemma GA entity 66.9 vs 71.1. The checker reads these cells as challenges; they are recorded as limits_scope.
- In the same study, AA exceeds QA for sentence-level GA (72.9 vs 66.5) and NPO (72.9 vs 67.2), and for RMU last token (64.5 vs 49.4; 2509.15631#AA-L8-RMUt). It also exceeds QA for the study's own method: 56.3 vs 37.9 on Llama3.1-8B (2509.15631#AA-L8-Ours) and 62.6 vs 48.2 on Gemma2-9B (2509.15631#AA-G9-Ours).
suggested_status.open_questions:
1. Does the Zephyr-7B RMU enhanced-GCG result reproduce with the same template and GCG step budget? Both studies attack the released cais/Zephyr_RMU, and 2608.22527 runs Łucki et al.'s (2409.18025's) enhanced-GCG code. The two results are 29.9 to 53.9 (2409.18025) and 0.3166 to 0.3637 (2608.22527). If it fails to reproduce, the optimized-prompt part on WMDP-RMU moves toward C.
2. Never-trained or retain-model controls under the same attack prompts. Soft-token attacks elicit about as much from never-trained Llama-2 as from unlearned models (2502.15836). GCG gives 0.000 even before unlearning (2611.05272). Unrelated dialogue contexts raise WMDP-Bio as much as related ones (2603.00823, unchecked: its source check was not returned). If attack prompts elicit the forgotten answers just as well from models that never learned them, the recoveries are artifacts (C).
3. Item-matched AA vs plain-QA probes on RWKU, at matched forgetting granularity. 2406.10890 (LLaMA3-8B-Instruct) finds AA above QA after GA and NPO. 2509.15631 (Llama3.1-8B) finds AA at or below QA for entity- and last-token-level GA and NPO, but above QA for sentence-level GA and NPO, RMU last token and its own method. Does AA-above-QA follow the depth of forgetting or the probe items?
4. Does any prompt-only attack by a group other than the method's authors bring TAR, RR, RepNoise, K-FADE or NPO+SAM back toward pre-unlearning accuracy? Third-party enhanced GCG does this for RMU+LAT (0.31→0.57, 2510.07626).
5. Recovery above 100B, on closed models with unlearned weights, and on reasoning models with standard methods. None of these is tested.
6. Interactive human red teaming against methods other than RMU, by a group with no author overlap with WMDP. Only 2408.15221 runs it, and it shares 4 authors with 2403.03218.

source.title: eight methods to evaluate unlearning
source.authors: Aengus Lynch; Phillip Guo; Aidan Ewart; Stephen Casper; Dylan Hadfield-Menell

original_result.setup: The study tested WHP, the Harry Potter unlearning model, using jailbreaks, Spanish and Russian prompts, and prompts with added book text or summaries.
original_result.result: Jailbreaks and added context partially restored Harry Potter familiarity, while Spanish and Russian prompts did not. Results were shown graphically without exact values.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: In-context examples recovered Enron information after DPO unlearning.

Five qualitative suffix-jailbreak examples showed no harmful leakage from OBLIVIATE.

Adversarial prompts and universal GCG suffixes failed to recover PISCES, ELM, or RMU knowledge.
Role-play, in-context examples, and poetry prompts barely increased harmful compliance after LLaVA unlearning.
Paraphrase and FigStep attacks produced no significant recovery after GD unlearning on LLaVA.
Jailbreaks and reformulated questions left harmful compliance low across tested unlearning methods.
Rephrased, perturbed, and noised queries failed to restore target tokens after attention-shifting unlearning.
Ring-A-Bell and name-free prompts failed to recover concepts erased by ACE.
Dialogue histories and five-shot context failed to materially recover knowledge from RMU checkpoints.
Jailbreak templates and GCG produced little or no recovery from BLADE-unlearned TOFU models.
BIO, META, and EMPTY prefills reduced output accuracy after NPO unlearning on Qwen-7B.
Optimized GCG prefixes left RAd models near chance on WMDP-Bio and Cyber.
Other languages, paraphrases, and forced language switching failed to restore forgotten knowledge.
Benign rephrasing produced little recovery in the specified NATO and Taiwan narrative-unlearning settings.
The tested prompt reduced FLAT scores and left CALIBURN scores at zero.
Random prefixes, jailbreaks, and paraphrases produced little recovery from CUSE-unlearned LLaVA.
Adversarial prompts failed to restore RWKU knowledge after GA and NPO unlearning.
Reformulation and extraction prompts produced no material recovery after NPO, PDU, or RMU.
By ROUGE, paraphrases failed to recover TOFU answers from Llama2-7B models that unlearned effectively.
An instruction-reversal prompt produced little recovery from DUET.
Enhanced GCG barely changed toxicity after REPO and tested RMU unlearning.
Paraphrases and adversarial prompts failed to recover knowledge in tested diffusion-unlearning settings.
Paraphrase and tested multi-hop probes largely preserved the unlearning measured by direct questions.
Jailbreak framings and paraphrases failed to recover GUARD-IT answers on Llama-3.2-1B.
Template paraphrases failed to increase personal-information recovery across tested LACUNA methods and models.
Held-out paraphrases did not reliably increase leakage in stable tested agents.
FocusOnKey produced recovery scores of 0.0 or 0.9 in tested AS and PALU settings.
French queries failed to expose facts unlearned in English with GradDiff-KL.
Multilingual queries and jailbreak wrappers left NSRU accuracy at or below post-unlearning accuracy with English queries.
Tested context, format, role-play, and dialogue attacks failed to restore Nullify's forgotten TOFU knowledge.
Contextual cues left forgetting near complete for HFRU, HFRU-SFT, and Mmunlearner.
Paraphrased and discriminative prompts preserved near-complete forgetting after encoder-only HFRU.
In-context examples failed to recover private information after GA, NPO, and RMU unlearning.
Five- and ten-shot examples left RepSelect recovery low, with some baselines also unchanged.
SIEVE's forgetting carried over to paraphrased queries on tested LLaVA and Qwen2-VL tasks.
Tested image-generation attacks left recovery low, close to what remained recoverable with explicit prompts.
Paraphrases recovered little forgotten knowledge under SAUL and the specified optimization variants.
In tested multimodal models, image inputs barely increased accuracy on forgotten material or reduced it.
Three benign instruction paraphrases failed to restore the suppressed MergeVLA-Goal skill.
Question and answer paraphrases barely altered TimeROME's suppression in diffusion language models.
Paraphrased TOFU queries did not reliably weaken forgetting under RMU or LUNAR.

On Llama and Gemma, DUET paraphrases left WGA recall near already-low levels from direct queries.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Prompt-only recovery on models above 100B parameters. The largest models with E rows are in the 10-100B range: Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE (2601.16905, 5-shot and poem prompts), Qwen3-32B (2608.04519, key-token repetition), QwQ-32B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (2609.38909, a behaviour rather than knowledge), Yi-34B in the original (2403.03218, GCG on one prompt per domain), and a transfer of perturbed prompts to Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (2409.18025 R55). GPT-4o appears only with inference-time unlearning, size not stated (2502.00406).
untested.basis: counts: E.studies_by_size has keys 1-10B (120), not stated (31), 10-100B (8) and <1B (3), with no '>100B'. E.coverage_by_operation.attack.by_size has 10-100B: 6 and no '>100B'.

untested.what: Prompt recovery from closed or API models whose weights were unlearned. GPT-4o and Gemini appear only with inference-time unlearning. In 2410.15267, in-context unlearning barely forgets there (USR 5.8% and 4.6%; 4.1% and 3.0% on rephrased queries), and the paper's RAG guardrail scores USR 99.2% and 99.5%, and 99.0% and 99.3% on rephrased queries. In 2502.00406, GPT-4o is unlearned only by ICUL, guardrail or ALU prompts, with no weight update.
untested.basis: counts: E.studies_by_family 'GPT (OpenAI API)': 1 and 'Gemini': 1; E.coverage_by_operation.attack.by_family 'GPT (OpenAI API)': 1, 'Gemini': 1. 2410.15267's untested line: rephrasing on closed models is uninformative because in-context unlearning never worked there.

untested.what: Supplying the forgotten facts themselves in context, rather than demonstrations, dialogue histories, retain-set questions or background that leaves out the answers, for WMDP hazardous knowledge or for TOFU/RWKU-style facts in autoregressive text LLMs. It has been done only for a TimeROME edit in masked diffusion LMs, where the answer is presented in context (2606.12841), and for Harry Potter familiarity on WHP models with book-text snippets or a summary in context (2407.15549 H03, H04, H07; five authors shared with 2402.16835). Two studies give context without the forgotten facts: 2402.16835 (E5–E7) put the first lines of Book 1 or a short or long summary in context, meant to leave out the Familiarity answers, and 2605.26992 prepends identity hints in a VLM, such as a profession or role, never the name.
untested.basis: Untested lines of arXiv:2411.12103 ('in-context provision of the forgotten information'), arXiv:2502.05209, arXiv:2512.18035 and arXiv:2603.11266 ('in-context provision of facts'). arXiv:2409.18025's untested line says in-context prompts were tried only qualitatively on RMU. No counts key separates prompt types.

untested.what: Other-language prompts on any reasoning model, and jailbreak or multi-turn prompts on reasoning models unlearned with standard methods. Jailbreak-style and three-turn extraction prompts are run only on GUARD, the study's own method (2609.21677). Standard methods on reasoning-distilled models get only paraphrase, reasoning-mode changes and thinking-trace prefills. 2601.09281 runs GA, GD, KL and PO on R-TOFU forget01 under paraphrase (Table 3) and reports their worst case over DefaultThink, ZeroThink and LessThink (MCS; forget01 GA 0.47, GD 0.46, KL 0.47, PO 0.56; no per-mode breakdown). 2605.18891 runs fixed-weight BIO, META and EMPTY prefills on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (seed 0: memorized and NPO K=100/400/800/1600; seed 1: NPO K=1600) and on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (memorized and NPO K=1600, where NPO did not lower out acc). A three-turn pushback on a reasoning model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B) targets a removed deception behaviour, not knowledge (2609.38909).
untested.basis: counts: E.studies_by_stage.reasoning: 1, and E.coverage_by_operation.attack.by_stage has no 'reasoning' key, although 2601.09281 and 2609.21677 attack DeepSeek-R1-distilled models (their rows carry stage 'fine-tuned' or 'not stated'). 2609.21677's untested line: no prompt attacks on GA, GD, KL, PO or R2MU. 2601.09281's untested line.

untested.what: Interactive human red teaming against any unlearning method other than RMU, or any model other than Llama-3-8B-Instruct. The only human multi-turn test is 2408.15221 (43 WMDP-Bio questions converted to free response; 51.2% success).
untested.basis: A search of packs E_1–E_4 finds human red teaming only in arXiv:2408.15221 (row r3). Its untested line says rephrasing, other languages and in-context information appear only as red-teamer tactics, with no per-tactic ASR. No counts key covers attack type.

wording_issues.issue: Most recoveries are partial against the pre-unlearning model. The best prompting attacks lift Llama-8B and Zephyr-7B LLMU/RMU to 0.29–0.40, against originals of 0.65–0.71 (2411.12103, e.g. r9 0.396 vs 0.696). On RWKU with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, multi-hop accuracy averaged over 12 methods is 27.0 (2-hop) against 97.2 before unlearning, and 33.9 (3-hop) against 84.1. Per method, 2-hop runs 18.7–44.5 and 3-hop 28.1–54.1 (GA 2-hop 23.8, r5) (2603.11266, Table 2). Near-full restoration appears only in particular cells. Cross-lingual RWKU probes bring EMMET on Llama3-Instruct to 0.461, against 0.456 before unlearning and 0.249 on its own simple questions (2601.08840 r26). Adversarial prefilling gives MOLLM 69.2% ASR on MUSE-Book, against a base of 70.5% (2604.15482). Several supporting studies give no pre-unlearning or never-trained reference.

Several results show knowledge that was never removed in the probed format, not knowledge removed and then brought back. After GA, NPO or MMUnlearner on Qwen3-VL-8B, target MCQ access changes by only 0.000–0.027 (2604.03114). After GA, KL or PO on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, four-choice MCQ stays at 62.7–65.0% against vanilla 64.4% (2510.22535). After English NPO unlearning, forget-probability ratios stay at 0.71–0.98 in nine other languages (2601.05641). For Llama2-7b with KL at step 30, Cloze probability (0.0187) matches the fine-tuned 0.0181 while default Q&A shows about 80% removal (2411.15477 r8). These rows record the unlearning step or an evaluation, not a separate attack.

Several recoveries need access beyond writing a prompt. Enhanced GCG prefixes are optimized with white-box access (2409.18025 R41: 29.9→53.9). REBEL's attacker sees the answer during its search (2602.06248: IDKNLL ASR 32.0→93.0). 2610.25731 runs a recovery audit, which is separate from its ACU defense. A fixed-weight team of three proposers and an aggregator, all output-supervised Native-only Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on TOFU forget10, feeds a frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct reader. Full ROUGE-L recovery is 41.8%. From the team's final answers alone it is 14.7%, and the reader given only the query reaches 1.8%. Retain-only retraining gives 21.4% (r1, r11). Soft-token attacks are white-box (embedding-space). They need about as many tokens for base Llama-2 not fine-tuned on TOFU (3.07 ± 3.25) as for unlearned models (IDK 3.40 ± 3.20), so they elicit completions whether or not the knowledge is stored (2502.15836).

The word covers attacks with very different outcomes. On RMU Llama-3-8B-Instruct, human multi-turn red teaming succeeds on 51.2% of 43 WMDP-Bio questions, and single-turn automated jailbreaks on at most 11.6% (2408.15221). A fixed, non-optimized jailbreak adds 2.5–9 TOFU forget-accuracy points (2404.18239). On RMU Zephyr-7B-β, Enhanced-GCG prefixes restore about 64% of the removed WMDP-Bio accuracy with the full forget set, and about 51% and 57% with 10% and 5% coresets (2504.10185, Table 3, pre-unlearning UE 35.35). For harmful-behaviour unlearning, manual, AutoDAN, GCG and prefilling attacks give Safe Unlearning ASR of 0–5 on both models. Under manual, AutoDAN and GCG attacks, RMU on Mistral gives 9.7–23.0 and Circuit Breaker on Mistral up to 10.0. PAIR gives 7–26 for Safe Unlearning, Circuit Breaker, DPO2 and RMU on Llama, and 42–52 for RMU on Mistral (2407.02855).

Results split by language, transfer direction and the language the facts were learned in. Translations are the best attack in several pairs. Telugu is best for Zephyr RMU on the authors' Biology set (0.298) and Bengali for Zephyr LLMU on WMDP-Bio (0.254). Hindi is best for Zephyr RMU (0.293) and Llama LLMU (0.374) on WMDP-Bio, and Farsi for Llama LLMU on WMDP-Cyber (0.178) (2411.12103). Spanish and French leave most Llama2-7b-chat methods unchanged, e.g. GA 88.30→87.00 in Spanish (2407.16997 R02). Take a Qwen model fine-tuned in EN/CH/RU. English-only DPO unlearning lowers CH (97) by 9 points and RU (87) by 4. Joint unlearning lowers EN by 96, CH by 94 and RU by 85. On a five-language model, joint unlearning lowers all five languages by 91–99 (2606.03291, Table 9). Transfer is asymmetric: GradDiff-KL gives RU→EN 0.20 against EN→RU 0.38 (2601.05641 r28).

Most in-context tests supply demonstrations, not the forgotten facts. 2604.22076 tests few-shot ICL (P2; k and demonstration source not stated) on LLaMA-3.2-3B with Enron+News PII. On the 20% split it lifts DPO to 30.61%, against a target of 29.94% and retrain of 4.95%, but leaves GA, NPO and RMU at 0–0.61%. On the 50% split DPO is at 0.00%. Unrelated MMLU Sociology histories raise WMDP-Bio about as much as target-related ones (Llama–NPO 25.29→31.26 related, 31.81 unrelated). Per the verdict, the same contexts raise MMLU for collapsed checkpoints (2603.00823, unchecked: its source check was not returned). Where the forgotten material itself is supplied, on WHP, book text leaves familiarity at 0.037 against a basic 0.044. A summary raises WHP-C to at most 0.116, against an original 0.575 (2407.15549). The only in-context tests in 2411.12103 are 5-shot prompts with answered MMLU questions from unrelated subjects. Its catalog record, not the paper, lists in-context provision of the forgotten facts as untested.

Meaning-preserving paraphrase and changes to the question's form behave differently. On GONE, held-out paraphrase probes give UE 0.971–1.000 where direct UE is 0.985–1.000 (Mistral GA, NPO, NEDS; Llama NEDS). For Llama NPO, paraphrase UE is 0.595 against 0.635 direct, while the inverse probe leaks at 0.209 (2603.12275). Multi-hop composition raises RWKU accuracy, averaged over 12 methods, from 20.1 (1-hop) to 27.0 and 33.9 (2603.11266). On ToFU 1%, paraphrase lifts FROUGE for Relearning-resilient from 0.01 to 0.44, the original model's level, and for RR+ALM from 0.02 to 0.34. Sharp Min–Max (0.12 ± 0.18) and SAUL (0.13 ± 0.22) stay low, as do Single/Dual AdamW with or without ALM, Sharp Min–Max+ALM and the SAUL ablations (0.02–0.05) (2608.16249). In SD v1.4 NSFW erasure, human-written I2P paraphrases sit 3–6 points above residuals for ESD, MACE, RECE, DoCo and Receler, but reach 71.83 for ConceptPrune (residual 10.32). Fixed MMA prompts give 27.57–75.7 ASR on RECE, DoCo, UCE, Receler and ConceptPrune, but 5.87, 2.40 and 1.03 on ESD, MACE and AdvUnlearn (2601.08623).

The version concerns targeted knowledge, but several tests measure other targets. One is harmful-output ASR (2407.02855). There the only knowledge measure is perplexity on harmful responses written by Llama-3-8B-Lexi-Uncensored (No Defense 1.71–1.96, Safe Unlearning 5.89e5–1.73e6, without attacks), with no accuracy-style knowledge test. Another is judged harmfulness, which its verdict says is not knowledge accuracy (2509.23362). Others measure regenerated image concepts in text-to-image models (2405.15234), or a deceptive caving behaviour judged by an LLM in 32B reasoning-style models (2609.38909). The statement does not say whether behaviours, image concepts or proxy scores count as 'it'.

The statement does not say whether 'it' was removed from the weights. Several recoveries undo unlearning that was done by prompts or guardrails. A reverse prompt lifts an in-context-unlearned Llama-3.2-3B from 4.52 to 37.62 R-Forget-500, near the base 39.99 (2601.21283 r12). Many-shot jailbreaking drops the PROMPT baseline's efficacy on Llama2-7b-chat from 82.94 to 5.00 (2407.16997 R14). The PROMPT guardrail on Mistral 7B Instruct scores 6 on normalized adversarial robustness (2410.17050 R12). In-context unlearning on GPT-4o and Gemini barely forgets (USR 5.8% and 4.6%), so rephrasing there cannot show recovery (2410.15267).

wording_issues.phrase: rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages or in-context information restore it
wording_issues.issue: The list leaves out prompt-only routes that do recover knowledge. It also names no unlearning method, though outcomes split by method. Adding the image at inference lifts InternVL3-8B NPO forget accuracy on Hateful Memes from 39.41 (text only) to 73.30 (2607.18615 r2). With no weight change, TAR-Bio-v1 (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) WMDP-Bio rises from 24.0 to 30.0 with the chat template alone. It rises to 39.8 with the BOS change alone and to 35.4 with both. GPT-4o or human extraction of free-form answers takes it above 45% (2412.07097). Repeating key tokens (FocusOnKey) recovers 51.9–95.0% in some method–model cells but 0.0 for AS on Qwen3-32B (2608.04519). Under the same few-shot ICL prompt (k not stated), on the 20% Enron+News split, DPO reaches 30.61% while RMU stays at 0.00% (target 29.94%, retrain 4.95%). On the 50% split both are at 0.00% (2604.22076).

method_sensitivity.what: Within one study and one attack, recovery differs sharply by unlearning method. On the 20% Enron+News split, few-shot ICL recovers 30.61% and 31.16% of PII from DPO (target model 29.94%, retraining 4.95%), but 0–0.61% from GA, NPO and RMU. On the 50% split DPO also gives 0.00/0.00 (LLaMA-3.2-3B; 2604.22076). Hindi filler raises ELM WMDP-bio accuracy by +0.18 to +0.25 but leaves RMU, TAR, PB&J, RR, GradDiff, RepNoise and RMU+LAT essentially unchanged (2506.10236). Dialogue-history contexts raise GA/NPO variants by 1–13 points, while RMU falls or stays flat (Llama-8B, Zephyr-7B; 2603.00823, unchecked: its source check was not returned). Enhanced GCG lifts DPO toxicity on GPT-2 Medium from 0.224 to 0.660 but REPO only from 0.206 to 0.208 (2602.23391).

method_sensitivity.factor: attack adaptivity, type and interaction format
method_sensitivity.what: Attack type and format change how much is recovered, or at what query cost, but more adaptive attacks do not always recover more. On RMU Llama-3-8B-Instruct, human multi-turn red teaming succeeds on 51.2% of 43 WMDP-Bio free-response questions, against 2.3–11.6% for each of six single-turn automated attacks (2408.15221). On SD v1.4 NSFW erasure, the fixed MMA prompt set beats the fixed I2P set for RECE, UCE and DoCo (e.g. UCE 38.67 vs 8.92 ASR) but not for ESD or MACE (e.g. ESD 5.87 vs 11.5). Optimized UnlearnDiffAtk gives 56.25 (ESD), 62.50 (MACE) and 82.81 (UCE) (2601.08623). On RWKU Llama-3-8B-Instruct 30-RT, AOA and ICL lift ROUGE-L from 0.456 to 0.805 and 0.804, while GCG does not help. On 30-GA (0.274; 0.794 before unlearning), ICL and AOA lower it (0.024, 0.157), while GCG and SoftGCG raise it (0.405, 0.437) (2505.23270). On CAE-unlearned Llama3, prefix injection, reverse query, multiple choice and cross-lingual prompts (0.230–0.300) exceed the 0.092 simple-question level; role play (0.074) and ICL (0.014) do not (2601.08840).

The probe's form decides whether residual knowledge shows. On GONE, inverse probes leak (Llama NPO UE 0.209, against 0.635 direct), while paraphrase probes do not (0.595) (2603.12275). On RWKU with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, average accuracy rises with hop depth (20.1, 27.0, 33.9). Aliasing adds +1.2 to +5.2 points, while step-by-step decomposition changes it by −1.4 to +1.2 (2603.11266). On TOFU with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, judge ASR is 45.0–70.0% for Multiple Choice suites and 60.0–82.5% for Structured CoT, against 72.5–95.0% for open-ended suites. RMU stays high under both (70.0 MC, 82.5 CoT) (2608.21606). On Qwen3-VL-8B, target MCQ access drops by 0.000 (GA, NPO) and 0.027 (MMUnlearner), while semantic free-form access drops by [0.040, 0.201] (GA), [0.040, 0.215] (NPO) and [0.135, 0.173] (MMUnlearner), lower/upper bounds. The cross-probe gap's 95% CI excludes zero only for MMUnlearner, [0.018, 0.217] (2604.03114).

method_sensitivity.factor: prompt template, BOS token, answer extraction and decoding
method_sensitivity.what: Evaluation choices that change no weights shift measured forgetting. TAR-Bio-v1 on Llama-3-8B-Instruct scores 24.0 on WMDP-Bio officially, 30.0 with the chat template and no BOS, 39.8 with no template and BOS, and 35.4 with both. With GPT-4o or human extraction of free-form answers (chat template) it scores above 45%. TAR-Bio-v2 scores 28.1 officially and 25.1, 24.3 and 25.1 under the same three changes; the text says v2 shows no spike under the chat template (Table 7; 2412.07097). Enhanced GCG on Zephyr RMU gives 29.9→53.9 when the template is not stated and 31.7→51.4 with the chat template. The verdict says the optimized prefixes are template-specific (2409.18025). Decoding: on the released WHP checkpoint with no audit prompt, Top-K sampling (temperature 2, K=40, 50 samples) gives average/max ROUGE 0.434/0.944, against 0.568 greedy; on Llama-3-8B-Instruct RWKU 30-RT, 0.441/0.922 against 0.456 greedy (Table 2, no rows; 2505.23270). On Llama-2-Who-is-Harry-Potter, greedy shows no keyword leakage, while sampling alone shows residual leakage (Fig. 3 only; 10.18653/v1/2025.emnlp-main.452).

method_sensitivity.factor: metric, scoring rule, judge and threshold
method_sensitivity.what: For the same attack, the scoring rule changes the measured recovery. Enhanced GCG on Zephyr-7B RMU raises max-letter-probability MCQ accuracy from 0.299 to 0.539 (base 0.644), and open-ended generation from 0.106 to 0.263 (base 0.597) (2506.00688). For AS on TOFU, rephrasing raises ROUGE-L from 0.02 to 0.11, while TR@50 goes only from 0.93 to 0.92 (2510.17210). A typographic attack on text-unlearned LLaVA-1.5-7B scores 69.2% by target string but 16.3% by LlamaGuard-4 (2607.16442). In 2411.12103, best-attack accuracy is 0.16–0.26 in several pairs, while accuracy on answered questions only is 0.27–0.54 (text, per the verdict).

The same method and attack give different recovery on different models. After LURK probing of WHP and Task Vector models, leakage is 4.0–8.4% on Llama2-7B (pretrained 32.7%) but 53.4–79.7% on Llama2-13B (pretrained 69.7%) and 67.3–84.9% on Llama3.1-8B (pretrained 54.6%). OPT-2.7B gives 0.0–5.2%, but its pretrained model also leaks 0.0% (2505.17160). Black-box 5-shot and poem prompts recover 11.5% on the unconstrained-RMU Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE (0.26→0.38, 0.37). A 'Dense Baseline' whose model and method Table 5 does not state recovers 2.5% (0.25→0.27, 0.28) (2601.16905). Under RWKU adversarial prompts, NPO exceeds the original on Gemma-7B-it (0.485 vs 0.471) but recovers only partly on Qwen2.5-7B (0.271→0.400, original 0.570) (2608.14229). In the math setting, jailbreak JB-1 gives the gradient-ascent baseline ASR of 10.7 (Llama-3.2-3B) and 42.0 (OLMo-7B), but 0.6 (Llama-3.2-1B) and 0.0 (OLMo-1B). Plain harmful questions give 0.0 on each, and in the medical setting all four rise (21.0–42.1) (2604.06154).

method_sensitivity.factor: query language, transfer direction and language of acquisition
method_sensitivity.what: Recovery through other languages depends on direction, language and how the facts were acquired. On Aya-Expanse-8B (TOFU), GradDiff-KL gives forget-probability ratios of 0.20 for RU→EN against 0.38 for EN→RU, and 0.14 for EN→FR against 0.65 for EN→Farsi. Plain GradDiff gives 0.25 (EN→FR) and 0.72 (EN→Farsi) (2601.05641). On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, GD with a Bengali source reaches 0.519 accessibility in English, against 0.009 in the reverse direction (text) (2609.05976). On LLaMa3-8B, English-source fake data unlearned in English is 94% removed in all query languages. About 45% persists in the source language after English unlearning of non-English data (2406.13748). Averaged over monolingual checkpoints (Tiny Aya Global, Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.2-3B), each fine-tuned and unlearned in one language, RMU removal is 91.1% under a query-only language change but 63.5% on native routes. A Hindi script change gives matched-form NLL advantages of 6.05 (SimNPO) and 8.26 (RMU) (16 runs, fixed 100 updates) (2609.40286).

What the attacker sees changes recovery. DUA suffix attacks on RWKU are weaker cross-query and cross-target than within-query (2408.10682). REBEL's evolutionary search, whose attacker sees the answer, reaches 60–93% ASR on several WMDP methods (Llama-3-8B-Instruct; 2602.06248). PDU's jailbreak prompts contain partial ground-truth information (2506.05314). In multi-agent teams of unlearned Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (TOFU forget10), a reader recovers 14.7% from final answers alone and 27.1 pp more when proposals are added. With the full trajectory it recovers 41.8 ± 1.4% (Qwen reader) or 45.0% (Mistral reader, against 2.1% query-only). With 7 proposers it recovers 49.4% (Qwen reader, stated in Section 4.2). Retain-only retraining gives 21.4% and the query-only Qwen reader 1.8% (2610.25731).

method_sensitivity.factor: dataset, knowledge domain and target concept
method_sensitivity.what: Recovery varies with the forgotten domain or concept. Enhanced GCG on Zephyr-7B recovers WMDP-Bio for NPO+MSE (27.0→52.9) and Adaptive RMU (29.4→43.9), but leaves WMDP-Cyber at ~25–33 for all methods against a base of 44.3 (text, Table 4; 2501.19202). Focus On Key recovers 9.5% (News), 14.3% (Books) and 63.4% (WMDP) of forgotten answers from RMU, and 27.7%, 42.9% and 60.3% from GAGD. Table 2 is not split by model (Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B) (2509.24675). Under WHP, authority framing lowers LLaMA-2-13B recall on Harry Potter (23.7%→18.3%) but raises it on U.S. Senators (30.3%→48.7%). WHP itself suppressed that model by about 18 pp on Harry Potter but 5 pp on Senators (Table 10) (2510.25732). In SD v1.4, Ring-A-Bell and UnlearnDiff recover the broad concept 'Dog' on UCE, ESD and CA, while English Springer, Van Gogh and Obama stay near 0 (2404.19382).

method_sensitivity.factor: training against the attack, unlearning regime and seed
method_sensitivity.what: How the unlearned model was trained changes prompt recovery. On MUSE-Book, adversarial-prefilling ASR is 70.5% for the base model, and 70.0% for GA and 70.5% for SimNPO, both trained on the study's first objective only. GA did not lower Forget there (36.9 vs base 32.1). Trained on all three objectives, SFT gives 1.5% and NGDiff 17.9%, but MOLLM 69.2%. ET, an in-context ensemble prompt on the base model with no training, gives 13.5% (model not stated; 2604.15482). In a catastrophic GA regime on Yi-6B (LR 6e-6, N=100), 5-shot, paraphrase and jailbreak prompts give F.Acc of 0.01–0.03, but in a collapsed model (2505.16831). On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B NPO adapters, the same BIO/META/EMPTY prefills lower answer accuracy on seed 0 (0.60→0.37/0.37/0.20) but raise it on seed 1 (0.68→1.00/1.00/0.98) (2605.18891). 2411.12103 reports stochastic training and checkpoint-dependent results.
